title: Test Organization
concept: Test modules organize tests alongside or separate from source code
why: A hundred test functions scattered across files become unmanageable. XIOM provides conventions for organizing tests: inline `@test` functions for quick unit tests, `tests/` directory for integration tests, and `#[cfg(test)]` conditional compilation to exclude test code from release builds.
theory: Three test organization levels in XIOM: (1) **Inline tests** — `@test` functions in the same file as the code, access private internals. (2) **Test modules** — `mod tests { ... }` blocks guarded by `#[cfg(test)]`, compiled only during testing. (3) **Integration tests** — files in `tests/` directory that test the public API as an external consumer would. Integration tests cannot access private items and each file is a separate crate.
tips: Use test modules for testing private internals
Use integration tests for verifying the public API contract
Keep integration test files focused — one file per major feature
common_mistakes: Putting integration tests in src/ instead of tests/
Forgetting `#[cfg(test)]` — test code ships in release
Importing private items in integration tests (compiler rejects this)
